is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles funestus.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports on CYP6P9a and the 6.5kb structural variant (Cyp6p9a/b 6.5kb-SV).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper provides genotype counts and associations for the 6.5kb SV and CYP6P9a in the F7 isofemale family (e.g., Table S2, Figure 4, and text on page 6).

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses laboratory colonies (FUMOZ from Mozambique and FANG from Angola) and their crosses (F2 and F7 generations). No field-caught mosquitoes were genotyped in this study.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study performing QTL mapping and BSA on laboratory-reared mosquito families.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study uses laboratory colonies, not field-collected samples with specific sub-country locations.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study uses laboratory colonies; no field collection dates are applicable.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study uses established laboratory colonies (FUMOZ and FANG) and describes new experimental crosses (F2 and F7 generations).

supplement.evidence: The necessary genotype data for the laboratory families is provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study performs QTL mapping and Bulk Segregant Analysis (BSA) on laboratory-reared F2 and F7 generations of Anopheles funestus, derived from crosses between the FUMOZ (resistant) and FANG (susceptible) colonies. It identifies a QTL (rap1) on chromosome 2 associated with alpha-cypermethrin resistance and validates the role of CYP6P9a and the 6.5kb structural variant in this resistance. As the study relies entirely on laboratory colonies and not field-collected populations, it is ineligible.
exclusion_reasons: The study does not use field-collected African mosquito populations; it uses laboratory colonies (FUMOZ and FANG) and their laboratory-reared progeny (F2 and F7 generations).
